record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: Can a polygonal billiard be mixing, necessarily in a case with at least one irrational angle, given that rational polygonal billiards are typically ergodic in fixed-direction restrictions but not mixing and irrational-angle polygonal billiards cannot have positive Lyapunov exponents?

evidence.quote: Very little is known about the case of irrational angles [43, 70], except that usual characteristics of chaoticity such as positive Lyapunov exponents are not possible here.
Open problem 6. Mixing property: Is it possible for a polygonal billiard (necessarily with at least one irrational angle) to be mixing?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a polygon $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (a bounded planar domain whose boundary is a finite union of line segments) and the associated billiard flow on the unit tangent bundle of $P$: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $P$ at unit speed and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting $\partial P$, with the dynamics undefined at corner trajectories. Equip the phase space with the natural invariant Liouville measure $\mu$ (normalized so that $\mu(P\times S^1)=1$). The billiard flow $(\phi_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ is said to be mixing if for all measurable sets $A,B$,
$$\lim_{t\to\infty} \mu(\phi_t^{-1}(A)\cap B) = \mu(A)\,\mu(B).$$
It is known that if all interior angles of $P$ are rational multiples of $\pi$ ("rational polygon"), then the directional flows are typically ergodic but not mixing, and that if at least one interior angle is an irrational multiple of $\pi$ then the billiard flow has zero Lyapunov exponents.

Question: Does there exist a polygon $P$ (necessarily with at least one interior angle that is an irrational multiple of $\pi$) whose billiard flow is mixing with respect to the Liouville measure?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to still be open. Weak mixing has been established for a dense set of polygons (Avila–Delecroix and earlier work), and recent numerical studies (2020–2024) provide strong numerical evidence that generic irrational-angle polygons (e.g., asymmetric irrational triangles) are mixing, but no proof of mixing for any specific polygonal billiard is known.

status_evidence.title: Weakly Mixing Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a weakly mixing billiard flow in a polygon; the set of polygonal tables with a weakly mixing billiard flow is dense.
status_evidence.claim: Weak mixing is known to hold densely, but strong mixing remains open.

status_evidence.title: Mixing Property of Symmetrical Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical evidence suggests that irrational polygonal billiards can be strongly mixing although never demonstrably chaotic.
status_evidence.claim: Recent numerical work supports mixing but does not prove it; the rigorous question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of billiards discussing open questions on ergodic and mixing properties of polygonal billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a mixing polygonal billiard is listed among open problems.
